ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the discrete spectra of six groups of Fourier series coefficients, labeled respectively as a_k, b_k, c_k, d_k, e_k, and f_k. In the lower-left figure labeled e_k, there is a positive central spectral line at k=0, and at k=±1 there are two negative spectral lines symmetric about the origin, with the remaining positions being zero. Then reason: The given signal is x_1(t)=2-2cos((2π/3)t), and its fundamental angular frequency is ω0=2π/3. Using cos(ω0t)=(e^{jω0t}+e^{-jω0t})/2, it can be written as x_1(t)=2-e^{jω0t}-e^{-jω0t}. Therefore the Fourier series coefficients have only c_0=2, c_1=-1, and c_{-1}=-1 nonzero. This is consistent with the three-spectral-line pattern of e_k in the figure, so e_k should be selected.

\begin{gathered}
x_1(t)=2-2 \cos \left(\frac{2 \pi}{3} t\right)
\end{gathered}
$$

Therefore the only nonzero Fourier series coefficients are the DC coefficient at k=0 with value 2 and the two first-harmonic coefficients at k=±1 with value -1. Then compare this three-stem pattern against the image; the lower-left plot labeled e_k shows exactly a positive central stem and two symmetric negative stems at k=±1, so select e_k.
